intro: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship 2027: French government funding for top international students - €1,181/month at master's level, €1,700/month at PhD level, plus travel and insurance. Institutions submit by 6 January 2027.
description:
Programme Overview

The Eiffel scholarship is the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' flagship instrument for attracting top international students to French higher education. It exists at two levels - master's and doctoral - and it is deliberately run through institutions: French universities and grandes écoles nominate the candidates they most want to keep. That design detail shapes everything about how you apply, because there is no direct application to Campus France.

At doctoral level the scholarship funds up to 36 months of thesis work in France; at master's level it funds M1-plus-M2 tracks up to 24 months (or 12 months where the institution nominates only the final M2 year). The programme covers four disciplinary clusters: science and technology, economics and management, law and political science, and - at master's level only - a limited set of other fields.

What the Scholarship Pays

Allowances and benefits
ComponentDetails
Master's allowance€1,181 per month, paid on top of direct services such as transport and cultural activities.
Doctoral allowance€1,700 per month.
TravelInternational return journey covered, plus an allowance for the first installation period.
InsuranceHealth insurance cover under the French student scheme and personal liability cover.
Not includedTuition fees are not paid by the Eiffel programme itself - many institutions waive or reduce fees for their Eiffel laureates, but that is decided by the host institution.

Eligibility

Key criteria for the 2027 campaign
CriterionRequirement
NationalityForeign (non-French) nationals; candidates with dual French citizenship are excluded.
Age - master'sUp to 29 years old under the limits published on the official programme page.
Age - PhDUp to 35 years old.
RouteOnly applications submitted by French higher education institutions are accepted; candidates cannot apply to Campus France directly.
Prior attemptsA candidate previously refused at master's level may reapply at doctoral level; laureates cannot receive a second Eiffel at the same level.

Application Timeline

How the campaign runs
StageDetails
Your move firstApply for admission to a French master's or doctoral programme in autumn 2026 and ask the institution to nominate you for Eiffel.
Institution deadlineEach institution sets its internal deadline well before the national cut-off - ask your contact at the university early.
Institution submissionFrench institutions submit nominated files to Campus France by 6 January 2027.
ResultsThe previous campaign published results from late March onwards; expect a similar window for 2027.

How to Approach the Application

Because the institution does the nominating, your real task is to convince a French department that you are worth their nomination slot, not to fill in a scholarship form. That means a strong admission file - grades, a focused study or research plan, and reference letters - plus an early conversation with the programme coordinator about Eiffel nomination. Candidates who contact departments between October and early December have the best chance of being considered, since institutions cap the number of files they forward.

About Campus France

Campus France is the national agency for international mobility and higher education promotion under the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. It administers the Eiffel programme end-to-end: campaign rules, institutional submissions, selection committee logistics and results publication.
